newsitem.title: INDIA: Laos seeks Indian help to match high Asian growth.
newsitem.headline: Laos seeks Indian help to match high Asian growth.

text.p: Laos, a late-comer to market reform, is seeking India's help to boost economic growth and emulate fast-growing southeast Asian neighbours, Laotian Prime Minister Khamtay Siphandone said on Friday.
"We hope cooperation with other countries, especially India, will help our country develop," Khamtay, who arrived on Thursday for a five-day visit, told reporters.

Laos has embarked on a reform programme to end state controls on the economy. The Asian Development Bank (ADB) said in a report last month that it had successfully established the basic elements of a market system.
Laos's economy grew 6.9 percent in 1996, compared with an average of 6.1 percent over the previous five years. It is forecast to grow 7.2 percent in 1997.
The ADB estimates annual growth rate at 8.0-8.5 percent between 1996 and 2000.

Khamtay was scheduled to attend a luncheon with President Shankar Dayal Sharma, meet vice-president K.R. Narayanan and address business leaders at the Confederation of Indian Industry later on Friday.
He was also due to hold talks with Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral after which the two countries were expected to sign cooperation agreements.
Officials said the two nations would explore the possibilities of cooperation in agriculture, transport, mining, hydro-electricity, irrigation, human resources and health.
Khamtay was the first head of government to meet Gujral after the Indian leader formed a centre-left coalition government on April 21.
Gujral, a communist-turned-social democrat, said relations with Laos had strong roots.
"Our cultures, our international outlook and our economic cooperation have always been close and will continue to be," Gujral said.
Khamtay was scheduled to visit industrial facilities at Bangalore and Buddhist holy places in the state of Bihar during the weekend.
He would round off his visit on Monday with a civic reception at Calcutta, capital of the communist-ruled state of West Bengal.
